does: Cooks flat foods on a wide, flat, heavy surface that is dry or only lightly oiled, so that they brown in speckles and spots on each face and stay soft within, without being fried in a pool of fat.
how: Heat the griddle well in advance, until it is evenly hot all over and a drop of water skips off it.
Wipe it with a thin film of oil, or leave it dry for a dough that holds its own fat.
Lay the food down flat and leave it still until the underside is spotted brown and it lifts easily.
Turn it and cook the other face, pressing lightly if it puffs.
Stack the finished pieces in a cloth so that they stay soft.

cues.text: Brown speckles on the underside, and bubbles or puffing on the top.
A toasty, bready smell, and not a burnt one.
A quiet sizzle when the food touches down.

mistakes.mistake: Putting the food on before the griddle is hot, so that it dries out and turns stiff.
mistakes.fix: Preheat it until it is evenly hot.

mistakes.mistake: Using too much oil, which fries the food and turns it greasy.
mistakes.fix: Wipe on only a thin film.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the finished food open to the air, where it dries and stiffens.
mistakes.fix: Stack it in a cloth to keep it soft.

variant_of.differs: The food lies on a flat surface that is dry or barely oiled and browns in speckles, where pan-frying cooks in a film of fat.
